content:
How to design a novel architecture with a novel RL algorithm.
Paper: AReaL: A Large-Scale Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning System for Language Reasoning
Challenges Switching between training and generation. Unequal output lengths. Inconsistent policies and stale data. Synchronous systems reduce the batch size per GPU, leading to memory-I/O-bound execution and poor scalability. System Architecture Interruptible rollout workers belong to the generation stage. The interrupt request is “Update Weights.”
Trainer workers accumulate data until the buffer reaches the batch size.
Rollout controller:
Read data and invoke generation → Send responses to the reward service → Store trajectories and rewards in the buffer → Update the model → Update the workers.
Equipped Algorithm For Staleness η represents the maximum permitted staleness in each training batch. Prioritize older trajectories from the data buffer to form a training batch. The rollout controller tracks both the generated samples N_r and policy version i from the parameter server. Favor a large η. In practice, use the parameters before updating as the proximal policy.
For Better RL Results Compared with PPO:
The outer importance ratio always uses the behavior policy as the denominator. The key choice is the trust-region ratio using the proximal policy. Implementation Details I Should Know CPU work: Rule-based computation and TCP-based data transfer. Separate threads and pipelining: Overlap GPU generation and CPU operations. Asyncio coroutines: Avoid mutually blocking waits in the rollout worker. Batching: A padding-free sequence-packing strategy coupled with a dynamic allocation algorithm. Dynamic Batching Instead of using a fixed batch size for sequences of different lengths, AReaL recombines sequences into batches through a greedy algorithm. Long sequences can cause OOM, while inefficient batching can underutilize memory.
Sequence Packing This is not this paper’s innovation. Concatenation enables padding-free execution with attention isolation.
Evaluation Designs Comprehensive comparisons against state-of-the-art open-source frameworks across model sizes. Strong-scaling analysis with varying compute resources. Ablation studies validating design choices. Baseline: veRL.
Ablation: Decoupled PPO.
Insight Allocating 75% of resources to inference and 25% to training demonstrated higher training throughput.
My Prospect of the Future MoE architecture optimization. More design work around the differences between training and generation. Preliminaries Generation involves autoregressive decoding, which requires efficient KV-cache management and optimized decoding kernels.
Training requires careful orchestration of data, tensor, and pipeline parallelism strategies.
Reference AReaL: A Large-Scale Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning System for Language Reasoning.
The AReaL paper figures reproduced in these notes are credited to the original authors. The PPO-Clip illustration is retained from the original notes.
summary: A second look at RL infrastructure through AReaL: asynchronous generation and training, interruptible rollouts, policy staleness, and implementation details.
title: The Second Glance with Infra: AReaL

content:
Through this paper, I understand the research pipeline in infra, especially in how to design an infrastructure for a specific popular training algorithm, which serves as a solid base for me to explore more in this area. By the way, I know a few professional explanations and code organization in this process.
Paper: HybridFlow: A Flexible and Efficient RLHF Framework
Basic Knowledge DP: Data Parallelism, more model replicas. TP: Tensor Parallelism, divide matrix into little matrices. PP: Pipeline Parallelism, attention for one GPU and MLP for another. Inference: One forward pass. Generation: Multiple forward passes. All-Gather: Collect data from all GPUs and each one then gets a complete copy of data. Reduce-Scatter: Collect and reduce data from all GPUs and then scatter part of reduced data to each GPU. Rank: Distributed process ID. Existing Works’ Shortcomings Single controller avoids complex point-to-point send and receive workflows, boosting more flexibility.
Analysis of RLHF (Take PPO as an Example) Actor training: Computation bound, more TP, more PP, less DP. Generation: GPU memory bound, more DP, less TP, less PP due to no gradient, no backward, no optimizer. Model resharding leads to memory redundancy. Code Realization APIs encapsulate distributed computation and support 3D parallelism, ZeRO, and PyTorch FSDP.
Python decorator: Additional functions without changing the code.
NCCL communication primitives collect and concatenate model parameters in each micro-DP group during the transition between training and generation.
Related Work Analysis DeepSpeed-Colocation: Actor training and generation in the same GPU, model resharding between training and generation. OpenRLHF: Each model placed on separate devices, two copies of generation and training models. NeMo-Aligner: Actor/Ref colocate, Critic-Reward colocate, same model for generation and training. Single controller: Insufficient for large GPU distribution. Multi-controller: Inflexible to implement various RLHF workflows. Key Design Single-controller in inter-node. Multi-controller in intra-node. Hierarchical API Use resource pools to manage GPUs. Configure models with different parallelism and then allocate devices. Asynchronous execution using data futures. 3D-Hybrid Engine Workflow: Switch Between Actor Training and Generation Dg is determined by p, t, pg, dg.
All-gather weights → Load prompts → Generate and all-gather responses → Partition weights → Model update → All-gather weights.
Zero Memory Redundancy All-gather within micro-DP groups enables both efficiency and no redundancy.
Auto Mapping Auto parallel + simulation + double nested loop for best mapping.
Nested loop:
Find best placements for actor, critic, reference, reward. Find best allocation for each group. Experiment Design Compare throughput across three RLHF algorithms. Compare throughput under different model placements, GPU counts, and model sizes. Compare the time of different transitions across GPU counts and model sizes. Break down actor model execution time under different parallelism strategies and model sizes. Design Principles Flexible. Efficient. Simple for users. Avoid a central bottleneck. Reference Guangming Sheng et al. HybridFlow: A Flexible and Efficient RLHF Framework, 2024.
The paper figures reproduced in these notes are from HybridFlow; credit belongs to the original authors.
summary: My first exploration of RLHF infrastructure through HybridFlow: controller paradigms, hierarchical APIs, the 3D-HybridEngine, and automatic device mapping.
title: First Meet Infra: HybridFlow
